replacement.title: Landing Page Visual Design
replacement.definition: The landing page must use an approved visual composition and aesthetic, including its dark treatment, hero presentation, typography, imagery, and accent choices, independently of responsive behavior, page chrome, and implementation handoff.

patches.decision_note: Landing-page visual design has its own approval and delivery trajectory but is absent from the inventory; it should not be represented solely through tokens, responsive behavior, or handoff.

replacement.title: Console Button Styling
replacement.definition: Console buttons must use an agreed treatment for color, shape, size, icons, and branded versus monochrome presentation.

patches.decision_note: Button styling has a distinct decision trajectory and was repeatedly identified as separate from the general Console shell.

replacement.title: Agent Cycle Diagram
replacement.definition: The agent solution page must include a production-ready cyclical process diagram with an agreed direction of flow.

patches.decision_note: The second solution diagram has content and acceptance criteria independent of the platform communication diagram, including its own clockwise-arrow decision.
The cited values and interaction states are explicitly provisioning-wizard-specific and are already represented by the wizard Requirement.

value_updates.page_reuse: Use the same footer across all website pages.

patches.decision_note: Footer reuse belongs here, but the general dark site theme is owned by the shared-page-treatment Requirement.

value_updates.site_theme: Maintain the dark theme of the landing page.

patches.decision_note: The shared visual theme belongs here, while header and footer structure must remain with their narrower page-chrome Requirements.
The message specifically defines treatment for the Sign In and Provisioning pages, and those changes are already owned by the two narrower Requirements.
The generic statement that the page looks good does not concretely verify the required Actia branding or final background treatment.

value_updates.look_and_feel_status: The client is comfortable with the finalized look-and-feel and layout.

patches.decision_note: The source reports a settled design direction with remaining shade and tone refinements, not an observed runtime failure.
